details.title: A Peak Element
details.statement_md:
Given `n` distinct integers, print the index (0-based) of **any** element that is strictly greater than both of its neighbours. Treat the position just outside either end of the array as `-∞`, so the first or last element counts as a peak when it beats its one real neighbour.

### Input
```
n
a1 a2 … an
```

### Output
The index of any one peak element. Several may exist; any is accepted.

### Constraints
- `1 ≤ n ≤ 200000`
- `-10^9 ≤ ai ≤ 10^9`, all distinct
- A peak always exists.

hints.body_md: You don't need to find every peak, only one. What happens as you walk the array comparing each value to the one right after it?
Walk left to right. The moment a value is bigger than the one after it, that position is a peak — the array rose into it and then fell away. If it never falls, the last element is the peak.
